description:
The pre-registered measurement. Before running: write the rule down in the example header (verdict thresholds from examples/README.md: good >= 2x over the optimized baseline; realistic size 1B rows; what is reported beside it: Rustler comparison, tick gap, peak memory, schedulers). Then, on the quiet-machine profile (defk-sgw.4 describes it): generate the 1B-row file (~13 GB; needs ~30 GB free with the output), run baseline, defk and the Rustler variants, best of 3 each, and record everything in examples/one_brc/README.md and as a DEFK_RESULT line that run_all.exs skips by default (a 1B run is minutes, not a CI check).

Also record: the generated C size and compile time for the kernel module (defk-6ag), the number of yields and promotions (__defk_stats__), and whether the result changes with DEFK_STRIP/DEFK_SLICE_US defaults.

Human-run because it needs the quiet machine and the disk space, and because the verdict is written by the owner.

Done when: examples/one_brc/README.md states the verdict with the numbers, and docs/language.md (defk-sgw.1) lists the constructs 1BRC added.
title: 1BRC: full-size run (1B rows) on a quiet machine and the workload verdict
